title: Weaveburst: session-weave burst shaping — latency vs cost slate (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures early benchmark notes and collateral copy for the Weaveburst concept — an experimental session-weaving + burst-shaping strategy aimed at reducing p90/p99 latency during short-lived microbursts while preserving amortized cost per query. Goal is to produce a short one-page slate and a small ASCII chart pack that the Console/design teams can iterate from.

Scope / assumptions:
- Workload: chat-style sessions (median prompt length 16 tokens, reply length 48 tokens), 70% short sessions (1-3 turns), 30% long sessions (>8 turns).
- Baseline: small-session dynamic batcher (current prod) on A100-sim nodes.
- Weaveburst mode: lightweight session affinity + adaptive prefetch of KV for predicted next-turns + micro-tiling to avoid cold-start prewarm.
- Cost metric: incremental GPU seconds per 1k queries normalized and $/1k estimate from infra pricing sheet (rough).
- Latency metrics: p50, p90, p99 request-to-first-token (ms) observed at the client trace point.

Raw summary (high-level):
- p90 improved by ~18-26% for microburst windows (10s spikes) with negligible impact on sustained throughput.
- p99 improved by ~9-14% in microburst scenarios but shows variability when hit rates of predicted next turns fall below 45%.
- Amortized cost per 1k queries increases slightly (~2-6%) in low-util periods due to prefetch overhead; decreases (~3-7%) for bursty periods because fewer fallback preempts and fewer full-model cold starts.

Topline ASCII charts (for slide text conversion)
1) p90 vs scenario (ms)
Scenario           | Baseline | Weaveburst | delta
------------------------------------------------
Sustained steady    |  120     |   118      | -2  (-1.7%)
10s microburst      |  210     |   162      | -48 (-22.9%)
30s surge           |  255     |   210      | -45 (-17.6%)

2) p99 vs scenario (ms)
Scenario           | Baseline | Weaveburst | delta
------------------------------------------------
Sustained steady    |  420     |   405      | -15 (-3.6%)
10s microburst      |  780     |   690      | -90 (-11.5%)
30s surge           |  920     |   810      | -110 (-12.0%)

3) Cost delta ($) per 1k queries (est)
Mode               | Baseline | Weaveburst | delta
------------------------------------------------
Quiescent (low QPS) | 0.92    | 0.98       | +0.06 (+6.5%)
Bursty (10s spike)  | 1.25    | 1.17       | -0.08 (-6.4%)
Sustained high QPS   | 1.10    | 1.12       | +0.02 (+1.8%)

Notes on instrumentation and how we measured:
- Synthetic replay from recent production session trace (sample segment from 2029-07-03). Replayed arrival times to a staging cluster with controlled node counts.
- Traces capture TTF1 (time-to-first-token) at API gateway span, and GPU seconds measured from runtime telemetry pipeline.
- Prefetch hit defined as: model KV warm present at decode start and no fallback path taken.
- Each data point is median of 5 runs (same seed) with 95% CI from run-to-run variance.

Detailed observations / tradeoffs:
1) Prefetch efficacy threshold: when predicted next-turn hit rate > 55% we see net latency + cost win on bursts. Between 40-55% it's primarily a latency win at modest cost (1-4%). Below 40% the prefetch overhead causes cost regression without consistent p99 improvements.
2) Handshake/Priming penalty: Weaveburst adds a small synchronous checkpoint at session resume to validate KV. If network RTTs to remote KVS exceed 8ms this checkpoint adds ~6-12ms tail. Consider async-validate fallback if region RTTs are variable.
3) Memory vs throughput: Weaveburst increases per-session resident KV footprint by ~20% — impacts multi-tenancy packing. For high-density tenants this changes slot packing heuristics and can reduce effective slots-per-GPU by 5-8%.
4) Failure modes: inaccurate next-turn prediction causes wasted prefetch and additional eviction churn. Observed in low-cohort-use-cases (background batch-style automation).

Operational knobs for Console UX (recommended to ship as toggles):
- Prefetch aggressiveness slider (0-100%) mapped to probability of prefetch. Default 60%.
- Adaptive fallback threshold: disable prefetch if consecutive misses > N (default 3).
- Burst-detection window length (5s/10s/30s) used to enable micro-tiling vs default batching.
- Memory-capacity budget per-tenant: soft cap to prevent packing regressions.

Open questions & follow-ups (for eng and SRE):
- Need a controlled experiment on racks in eu-west to verify RTT penalty for remote KVS (INF-5794).
- How does Weaveburst interact with existing quantized fast paths? initial testing shows similar speedups but must rerun Q4 quant profiles. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-profiles/pulls/58)
- UX: product wants a single-sentence description and a 1-row console card showing "burst latency saving" and "cost delta". Draft copy below.

Draft product copy (1-liner for console):
"Weaveburst — smart session weaving that shapes short bursts to cut p90/p99 during spikes while keeping costs in check (tunable)."

------------------------------------------------------------------------

R-103  | 10s microburst | 140     | 210     | 780     | 10        | 1.25       | baseline

R-206  | 30s weaveburst | 150     | 210     | 810     | 12        | 1.30       | partial tiling

Quick recommendations (engineering/product):
- Run regional RTT probe (INF-5794) and gate the synchronous KVS validation based on region LATENCY percentiles.
- Add a conservative default on Console (prefetch aggressiveness = 50%) and expose advanced controls for Dedicated customers.
- Start an A/B with a small set of bursty tenants (billing tier: dev+growth) for 4 weeks, collect p90/p99 and per-tenant cost deltas.

Who to ping next:

- 2w: iterate on prefetch heuristics and conservative default.
- 4w: gated A/B with selected tenants, dashboard telemetry.
